newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-UK's Dawson ready for expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-UK's Dawson ready for expansion.

text.p: After two years of tough trading conditions, Scottish textiles company Dawson International said on Wednesday it was ready to look for "positive acquisitions" aimed at enhancing shareholder value.
"We have turned around the corner, for the first time we find us in a position from where we could look ahead," Peter Forrest, Dawson's managing director said in an interview.

Dawson, which has a wide portfolio of operations including marketing branded knitwear, reported a moderate increase in pre-tax profits to 12.5 million stg in the year to March 1997, from 4.3 million stg in the previous year.
The company's basic earnings per share stood at 5.4 pence.
Forrest pencilled the company's strengthening balance sheet which showed a net cash inflow of 30 million stg.
"The gearing is down to 15 pct, it does give us some breathing space to look outside and think of some positive acquisitions," he said.
Separately, the company's chairman, Derek Finlay, described the 1996/97 results as the turning point in Dawson's fortunes.

"Looking ahead, I am increasingly confident that provided the competitive position of our UK operations is not eroded by the continued strengthening of sterling, Dawson International will make further solid progress in the current year," he said.
In the current year, Forrest said, the company's operations were "looking okay" with most areas slightly up on the previous year.
Cost-cutting, mostly done through the closure of its loss-making woolcombing operation, has been one of the main factors behind the company's improvement.
Forrest said the company did not rule out further disposals in the future. "We are constantly looking at it," he said.
The company's cashmere division, Joseph Dawson, is expected to improve further after its dehairing unit in Mongolia starts operations by September.
The start of this plant would ensure long-term supply to raw cashmere fibre and improve the cashmere division's profit margins, Forrest said.
